text.title: JPA / Hibernate Worked Examples
text.summary: Worked fragments for the mapping, repository and transaction rules — the justification comment, @Version, parameterised dynamic queries, narrow-repository segregation and service-owned transactions. Full file bodies live in templates/.

section.title: Entity mapping — audit timestamps, @Version, justified associations

example.note: Satisfies `audit-timestamps`, `optimistic-locking-on-editable-aggregates` and `justified-cascade-fetch`. `CascadeType.ALL` is permitted on `orders` only because the comment states the ownership analysis; strip the comment and the mapping is blocked.

section.title: Repository — JOIN FETCH, parameterised filtering, safe bulk update

example.note: `@Modifying` requires `@Transactional` on the calling service method — without it Spring Data throws `TransactionRequiredException`. Add `JpaSpecificationExecutor` only when dynamic filtering is genuinely required.

section.title: Narrow repository — segregating what services may call

example.note: Satisfies `narrow-repo-interface` and `dto-projection-on-reads`. `OrderRepository` carries no `deleteAllInBatch()` and no `findAll()`; `OrderRepositoryJpa` is the Spring Data implementation and never appears in a service signature.

section.title: Service — transaction ownership and DTOs across the boundary

example.note: Satisfies `service-owns-transaction-boundary` and `dto-projection-in-controllers`, and closes the `optional-get-without-context` failure mode. Nothing but DTOs leaves the class, so `lazy-outside-tx` cannot fire.
